security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, placeholder Azure URLs, and documented environment variable usage. I found one content-level risk: examples print configuration values, which can expose secrets if copied into production logging.

remediation.issue: Configuration values are printed in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace full value logging with redacted examples and warn users not to log secrets or Key Vault resolved values.

remediation.issue: Connection string authentication is shown beside DefaultAzureCredential.
remediation.suggestion: State that DefaultAzureCredential and RBAC are preferred, and connection strings must stay in secret stores or environment variables.

remediation.issue: Installation commands are presented without supply-chain guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Advise users to verify package names, lock dependencies, and review npm install scripts in regulated environments.

content.user_title: Manage Azure App Configuration in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Application teams need consistent configuration, feature flags, and refresh behavior across TypeScript services. This skill provides focused Azure App Configuration patterns for setup, SDK use, labels, snapshots, and Key Vault references.
actual_capabilities: Shows package choices for low-level Azure App Configuration SDK, provider loading, and feature management.
Demonstrates TypeScript authentication with DefaultAzureCredential or an Azure App Configuration connection string.
Covers create, read, update, delete, lock, and unlock operations for configuration settings.
Explains provider loading, key prefix trimming, dynamic refresh, and Express middleware refresh patterns.
Documents feature flag creation, targeting evaluation, labels, snapshots, and key type imports.
Includes guidance for Key Vault references and secret refresh intervals.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not executable automation or a complete sample application.
It does not validate Azure permissions, network access, or resource names for a specific tenant.
It assumes TypeScript projects can install Azure SDK packages from npm.
It does not replace security review for secrets, logging, or production rollout rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize App Configuration Setup
use_cases.description: Plan package selection, authentication, labels, and environment separation for TypeScript services using Azure App Configuration.

use_cases.title: Add Dynamic Runtime Refresh
use_cases.description: Use provider loading, refresh intervals, and middleware patterns to keep application settings current without redeploying.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Flag Rollouts
use_cases.description: Create feature flag guidance with targeting, groups, labels, snapshots, and rollback-friendly release controls.

prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Azure App Configuration to a TypeScript service. Include package choices, authentication options, and required environment variables.

prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to load app settings with the Azure App Configuration provider, trim key prefixes, and access settings in a TypeScript app.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Feature Flags
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript feature flag setup with Azure App Configuration, targeting rules, user groups, and refresh behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production plan for labels, snapshots, Key Vault references, refresh intervals, RBAC, and safe logging practices.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential with role-based access when possible.
Use labels and snapshots to separate environments and protect releases.
Avoid logging full configuration values, especially secrets and Key Vault references.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding connection strings or endpoints directly in source files.
Listing and printing every configuration value in production logs.
Using feature flags without documented ownership, labels, or rollback rules.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript guidance and examples. You still control package installation, code changes, and Azure access.

faq.question: Can it use DefaultAzureCredential?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance prefers DefaultAzureCredential for endpoint-based authentication when Azure identity and RBAC are available.

faq.question: Does it cover connection strings?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents connection string usage, but secrets should stay in secure environment variables or secret managers.

faq.question: Can it help with dynamic refresh?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers provider refresh options, refresh intervals, callbacks, and middleware-style refresh patterns.

faq.question: Does it support feature flags?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes feature flag creation, provider loading, targeting context, users, groups, and refresh settings.

faq.question: Does it replace Azure testing?
faq.answer: No. You must still test permissions, labels, refresh behavior, and production safety in your Azure tenant.
